fl-hillsborough-2026-bocc-d7-wostal-josh.name: Joshua Wostal
fl-hillsborough-2026-bocc-d7-wostal-josh.bio: Hillsborough County Commissioner since 2022, general contractor business owner, and 10-year U.S. Navy veteran.

positions.stance: Pledges to "End Wasteful Spending" in the county budget, citing $235 million in property taxes going to unaccountable non-government entities.
Pledges to "Stop the Tax Hikes," saying he voted against four property tax increase attempts.
Pledges to "Fix Our Crumbling Infrastructure," including redirecting funds to roads, sidewalks, and fire safety without raising taxes.

fl-hillsborough-2026-bocc-d7-rodriguez-a.name: Aileen Rodriguez
fl-hillsborough-2026-bocc-d7-rodriguez-a.bio: Public affairs executive and principal of AR Public Affairs & Strategic Solutions.

positions.stance: Will tackle housing and transportation costs so teachers, first responders, and young families aren't priced out of the community.
Will fight to reinvest tax dollars directly into the neighborhoods most impacted by development so infrastructure keeps pace with growth.
Will hold developers accountable and ensure they "pay their fair share," preserving the county's character from "reckless sprawl."
Will support funding the fire and police stations a growing population needs to ensure fast response times for every resident.

fl-orange-2026-clerk-of-courts-johnson-r.name: Roberta Walton Johnson
fl-orange-2026-clerk-of-courts-johnson-r.bio: General Counsel for the Orange County Clerk of Circuit and County Courts, where she established and led the Lydia Gardner Self Help Center.

positions.stance: Will lead a customer-centered Clerk's Office that "meets people where they are and removes barriers to accessing the courts."
Will champion innovation and technology-forward service so the office is efficient today and prepared for future needs.
Will safeguard court records, protect public dollars, and uphold court data quality.
Will lead community education partnerships that help residents understand how their courts work.

ny-erie-2026-county-clerk-meyer-steven.name: Steven G. Meyer
ny-erie-2026-county-clerk-meyer-steven.bio: Williamsville Village Trustee and small business owner.

positions.stance: Will restore credibility to the County Clerk's Office, bringing transparency and accountability from Day 1.
Will modernize the office's constituent services to improve satisfaction and create more transparent processes.
Will expand the Clerk's Office's access and presence across Erie County so residents "get what we pay for."

ny-erie-2026-county-clerk-kearns-michael.name: Michael P. Kearns
ny-erie-2026-county-clerk-kearns-michael.bio: Erie County Clerk; former New York State Assemblymember and Buffalo Common Councilmember.

positions.stance: Says her latest county budget passed with "no new taxes, fines, or fees" and that she has not raised property taxes in 15 years.
Ensures County services remain accessible regardless of immigration status and prohibits County property and personnel from use in civil immigration enforcement.
Focuses on "creative and innovative solutions" to ensure residents have access to quality medical and mental healthcare, including medical debt relief.

il-cook-2026-assessor-hynes-pat.name: Pat Hynes
il-cook-2026-assessor-hynes-pat.bio: Lyons Township Assessor since 2021 who spent two decades at the Cook County Assessor's Office.

positions.stance: Will restore field inspectors to the staffing levels that existed before the incumbent cut their ranks.
Will end the practice of ignoring building permit data shared with the Assessor's Office.
Will invest in training so frontline staff can provide accurate information quickly and consistently.
Wants to return to generally accepted appraisal principles and "make the Cook County Assessor's Office boring again—predictable, professional, and accurate."
Will start a public-facing Department of Economic Development working with small businesses, neighborhood associations, chambers of commerce, and labor.

il-cook-2026-mwrd-6yr-pennington-michell.name: Michelle Pennington
il-cook-2026-mwrd-6yr-pennington-michell.bio: Real estate investment business owner since 2007.

positions.stance: Says every MWRD dollar should trace directly to its two jobs: cleaning wastewater and preventing flooding.
Says MWRD should provide a complete public accounting of the Harvey stormwater project before it advances further.
Proposes cutting the 29-person legislative affairs office to a lean team of 12 to 15, with savings going to flood infrastructure.
Says community events unrelated to water infrastructure do not belong in the MWRD budget.
Would consolidate technical internships into the existing apprenticeship program and eliminate the separate diversity internship program.

il-cook-2026-mwrd-6yr-rueckert-timothy.name: Timothy E. Rueckert
il-cook-2026-mwrd-6yr-rueckert-timothy.bio: Former highway commissioner and criminal investigator.

positions.stance: Protecting Lake Michigan and waterways from pollution, combined sewer overflows, and industrial discharge.
Demanding transparent budgets, competitive bidding, and "an end to the patronage culture" that drives up costs.
Investing in green infrastructure, stormwater management, and long-term solutions that protect communities from flooding.
Bringing independent oversight and a commitment to open government to the MWRD.

il-cook-2026-mwrd-6yr-shestokas-jill.name: Jill B. Shestokas
il-cook-2026-mwrd-6yr-shestokas-jill.bio: Former MWRD Public Affairs Director and principal of the Thomas & Joyce public-affairs consultancy.

positions.stance: Prioritize communities facing repeated flood damage and measure whether protection actually reaches them.
Set clear goals, deadlines, and responsibility so residents can see where projects stand and when relief will arrive.
Use modern tools alongside proven infrastructure to meet "today's storms—not yesterday's standards."
Connect borrowing and spending to projects that are ready, necessary, and capable of delivering clear public value.

il-cook-2026-mwrd-6yr-brady-davis-precio.name: Precious Brady-Davis
il-cook-2026-mwrd-6yr-brady-davis-precio.bio: MWRD Commissioner since 2023 and Chief Strategy Officer at the Center on Halsted; former Sierra Club regional communications director.

positions.stance: Leading efforts to protect communities from flood damage.
Leading efforts to modernize water systems to be sustainable and energy-efficient.
Leading efforts to build climate-resilient infrastructure.
Would stop leasing MWRD land to polluters who endanger waterways, wildlife, and public health.
Would direct flood-relief resources to the South and West sides, which she says are hit hardest but receive the least help.

il-cook-2026-mwrd-6yr-corral-sepulveda-e.name: Eira Lizeth Corral Sepúlveda
il-cook-2026-mwrd-6yr-corral-sepulveda-e.bio: MWRD Commissioner with over 15 years of experience in civic engagement, local government, and environmental leadership.

positions.stance: Engages neighborhoods equitably in building resilience against climate change and protecting residents from floods.
Advocates for MWRD to support greater investment in green infrastructure and ensure projects prioritize equity.

il-cook-2026-mwrd-6yr-mcelroy-kirkwood-b.name: Beth McElroy Kirkwood
il-cook-2026-mwrd-6yr-mcelroy-kirkwood-b.bio: MWRD Commissioner appointed in December 2024, ESL teacher in Orland School District 135, and Moraine Valley Community College Board chair.

oh-cuyahoga-2026-executive-ronayne-chris.name: Chris Ronayne
oh-cuyahoga-2026-executive-ronayne-chris.bio: Cuyahoga County Executive; former Cleveland Planning Director and Chief of Staff.

oh-hamilton-2026-commissioner-0101-owens.name: Meeka Owens
oh-hamilton-2026-commissioner-0101-owens.bio: Cincinnati City Councilmember with prior work in the nonprofit and community development sectors.

positions.stance: Supports prevention-focused housing strategies using predictive data and early intervention to address instability before eviction or homelessness.
Supports Access to Counsel programs providing legal representation for tenants facing eviction.
Supports climate action that improves affordability and public health, prioritizing neighborhoods with the highest pollution rates.
Emphasizes sustainable funding, transparent processes, and performance-driven use of public dollars, with equitable, neighborhood-rooted growth.

oh-hamilton-2026-auditor-miranda-jessica.name: Jessica E. Miranda
oh-hamilton-2026-auditor-miranda-jessica.bio: Hamilton County Auditor, small business owner, and former Ohio House District 28 Representative.

positions.stance: Will uphold accurate, fair property valuation in adherence with state regulations so property owners can trust the results.
Committed to making sure taxpayers can easily find information online about how tax dollars are used.
Committed to "leveraging technology and innovation to streamline operations and improve service delivery."

ga-fulton-2026-commchair-tatum-eric.name: Eric J. Tatum
ga-fulton-2026-commchair-tatum-eric.bio: Georgia attorney since 2011 practicing family, juvenile, and adoption law; CFO and partner at Banks, Stubbs & McFarland, LLP.

positions.stance: Conduct full audits across major spending areas, "rein in property taxes," and ensure taxpayers receive the services they pay for.
"Fix the jail crisis" and prioritize public safety and courthouse funding while building trust between law enforcement and neighborhoods.
"We must abolish human trafficking" so predators have nowhere to hide in Fulton County.
Fix election processes, ensure government is accountable to the people, and lead with integrity.

ga-fulton-2026-commchair-ivory-mo.name: Mo Ivory
ga-fulton-2026-commchair-ivory-mo.bio: Fulton County Commissioner for District 4; attorney, law professor, entrepreneur, and media personality.

positions.stance: Will work to ensure courts are properly funded, uphold constitutional standards, and protect safety and dignity for everyone.
Will strengthen public healthcare capacity and expand care where it's needed most.
Will ensure Fulton County elections are "well-run, accessible, and fully supported."
Will open up the budget process, strengthen oversight, and make sure investments reflect residents' priorities.

nc-mecklenburg-2026-commissioner-at-larg.name: Leigh Altman
nc-mecklenburg-2026-commissioner-at-larg.bio: At-Large Mecklenburg County Commissioner since 2020; former public-interest attorney and Georgia Assistant Attorney General.

positions.stance: Fighting "for improved mass transit."
Fighting for "better funded parks and greenways."
Fighting for "high quality public schools."
Fighting for "strong economic development."
Fighting for "transparency in government."
Improve communication of county services to residents.
Improve services and technical assistance to small businesses, "adding global opportunities."
Partner to diminish food insecurity across the county.
Focus on services to families that align with improved educational outcomes, especially mental health.
Says public institutions should collaborate with employers and community partners to close the workforce skills gap.
Says the goal should be livable communities with homeownership opportunity: "If you work here, you should be able to live here."
Says neighborhoods should have equitable access to county recreational assets and clean water and air "should not depend on one's zip code."
Supports inclusive economic growth through high-quality workforce programs and criminal justice reform with smart local economic strategies.
